articles.summary: Hi! I'm Rick Lane, and you might remember me from such columns as Reality Bytes , RPS' erstwhile monthly goggle at the world of virtual reality . I've spent the last couple of years trapped between the second and third dimensions, my flattened body doomed to forever spin to face the camera. But RPS has whipped out its bicycle pump and popped me back into stereoscopic 3D, so I can seek revenge tell you all about the state of VR in 2026. And boy, what a state! The headlines make for grim reading. VR headset shipments are in decline . Notable VR studios are either laying people off or being shut down outright . articles.title: How AI Agents Are Changing Software Development
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence is rapidly moving beyond simple chatbots and code completion tools. Modern AI systems can now understand context, use external tools, interact with APIs, analyze large amounts of information, and perform multi-step tasks. This evolution has led to the rise of AI agents , systems designed to complete tasks rather than simply respond to individual prompts. An AI agent typically combines a large language model with memory, tools, and a reasoning or planning mechanism. Instead of receiving a question and immediately generating an answer, the agent can determine what information it needs, select an appropriate tool, execute an action, evaluate the result, and continue working until the task is completed. For developers, this creates an entirely new way of building applications. An AI-powered customer support system, for example, can retrieve customer information from a database, search documentation, check an order status through an API, and then generate a personalized response. articles.title: Building Scalable Web Applications with Modern Backend Architecture
articles.summary: Modern web applications are no longer simple collections of frontend pages and backend endpoints. As applications grow, developers need to think about performance, scalability, security, maintainability, and reliability from the beginning. A well-designed backend architecture allows teams to add new features without turning the codebase into a difficult-to-maintain system. A typical modern application consists of several interconnected layers. The frontend communicates with backend APIs, the backend handles business logic, and databases store persistent information. Additional services such as caching systems, message queues, authentication providers, and object storage can be introduced as the application becomes more complex. Keeping these responsibilities separated makes the system easier to scale and debug. For JavaScript developers, Node.js is a popular choice for building backend services because it allows developers to use JavaScript across the application stack.
